summary: AE+SE walked through Redwood Console usage analytics and per-route dashboards. Focus on how console surfaces cost per-route, token burn, model/variant comparisons, and options for Dedicated capacity and caching to reduce unit cost. Customer concerned about latency targets for storefront features and security (VPC/SOC2). Agreed to run a 1-week benchmark on sample traffic and follow up with pricing and SOC2 docs.
transcript: [00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro, I'm Alex on the account team and Priya is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?

[00:08] Maya Thompson (Heron): Good, thanks. Excited to see the console. We want to understand cost mapping by feature — product pages, search, recommendations — and how Redwood can help keep latency under 200ms for critical flows.
[00:24] Alex Chen: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll cover. Priya will show the console and per-route dashboards, then we'll talk tradeoffs and next steps. Priya?

[00:32] Priya Patel (Redwood SE): Thanks Alex. I'll share my screen — give me a sec. (screen share) Alright, starting at the top: this is the usage analytics homepage. You can see token volume over time, cost trends, and top routes by cost and latency.
[00:50] Daniel Park (Heron): Quick q: are those cost numbers real-time or delayed? We need near-real-time for SRE alerts.

[00:57] Priya Patel: Good question. By default they're updated every 5 minutes for Hosted, with higher fidelity for Dedicated if you enable streaming telemetry. There's also an events endpoint you can pipe into your observability stack.
[01:12] Sana Khan (Heron CFO): The per-route cost — what drives that mainly, tokens or model choice?

[01:18] Priya Patel: It's primarily tokens and model latency. On this example dashboard you can filter by model variant, time window, and route tag. See this column — cost per 1k tokens — and here is the breakdown by route. So product pages are high token count because of long context, search is many short calls so higher request count but lower tokens per call.
[01:45] Maya Thompson: Can we tag routes automatically from our API gateway or do we need to add headers?
[01:50] Priya Patel: You can do both. We support automatic route inference for common frameworks, but adding a header like x-redwood-route is the simplest and most reliable.
[02:02] Alex Chen: Just to align, you said latency target 200ms for storefront — is that tail P95 or P99?
[02:08] Maya Thompson: P95. P99 is nice but lower priority right now.
[02:12] Alex Chen: Great, that helps. Priya, could you click into the per-route detail for the "product_page" route?

[02:18] Priya Patel: Yep. Here we have a per-route timeline, tokens per request, avg latency, error rate, and cost. Notice the model split — we've got requests hitting rwd-3b-quant and a larger rwd-13b float variant. The console shows estimated cost delta if you move to a quantized variant or enable prefix cache.
[02:44] Daniel Park: That 'prefix cache' — is that the KV cache you mentioned in the docs? We've had trouble with KVcahce invalidation across replicas before.

[02:51] Priya Patel: It's the KV cache, yep. We handle cache invalidation via route-level keys and optional TTLs. For Dedicated we also provide sticky routing to keep hot KV consistent. Sorry — my transcribe shows K V cache sometimes, transcription error.
[03:10] Maya Thompson: One of our concerns is model fallbacks during peak — we can't have users hit 800ms when auto-scale kicks in.

[03:16] Priya Patel: Understood. Our Smart Routing policy can do route-level fallbacks: e.g., product_page tries rwd-13b-quant, if latency approaching threshold fallback to rwd-3b-quant or a cached response. You can set per-route SLOs to trigger fallbacks automatically.
[03:35] Sana Khan: From a cost perspective, what kind of savings are realistic if we move parts of traffic to Cached + 3b quant?

[03:41] Priya Patel: It depends on hit rate. If you get ~30-40% prefix hits for product descriptions you could see 20-35% cost reduction. For search, batching short queries together can yield additional savings. We'll model this in the benchmark we propose.

[04:00] Alex Chen: I'm going to show the cost breakdown panel — Priya, bring that up. Here you can compare cost by model over time and simulate hypothetical changes, like swapping rwd-13b -> rwd-13b-quant or enabling caching. This is great for exec reporting and for Sana to show CFO-level impact.
[04:22] Sana Khan: The simulation tool — does it use our actual token distribution or a synthetic profile?

[04:27] Priya Patel: If you upload telemetry we use real distribution; if not, we fallback to modeled distributions per route. Uploading your telemetry gives the most accurate per-route cost projection.
[04:40] Maya Thompson: About security — we need VPC peering and customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). Are those available for Dedicated?

[04:47] Alex Chen: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private deployments have HSM/KMS integrations. We'll share the SOC 2 and network whitepaper after this call. (note: SMAL spelled SMAL in some earlier docs, apologies)
[05:02] Daniel Park: Does the console show token-level attribution for individual users or is it aggregated? We need to link costs back to product owners and teams.
[05:10] Priya Patel: You can break down by route, team tag, or user id if you send the metadata. There's also export to CSV and a per-route API to pull raw usage events into your billing system.
[05:25] Maya Thompson: Can we set alerts when a route's cost spikes unexpectedly?
[05:29] Priya Patel: Yep — alerting on percent-change, absolute token delta, or latency regressions. Integrates with PagerDuty and your webhook endpoints.
[05:40] Alex Chen: Quick qualification: what's your expected QPS for search and product_page in peak?
[05:45] Maya Thompson: Search peak ~120 qps, product_page bursts up to 35 qps, average lower. We're experimenting with caching for caching for product snippets to reduce token usage.

[05:58] Priya Patel: Good to know. For 120 qps search you might want to consider batch windows or lower-latency model endpoints; Dedicated makes sense once sustained throughput crosses ~50-60 qps depending on model mix.
[06:15] Daniel Park: If we go Dedicated, what's commit look like — monthly? annual? We need pricing ranges to model in our infra budget.

[06:22] Alex Chen: Dedicated is typically reserved monthly or annual capacity. I'll include ranges in the deck — small/medium/large pools and burst tier pricing. We'll also show a blended unit cost estimate so you can run internal chargebacks.
[06:35] Maya Thompson: We also need a smoke test for hallucinations/regression when you change quantization. How do you guard output quality when switching models?

[06:42] Priya Patel: Great question — Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. You can pin golden prompts and run A/B on variants; the console will surface BLEU-like metrics and human-review flags.
[06:58] Alex Chen: I'll pause for questions. Any other regulatory constraints?
[07:02] Sana Khan: Data residency — some EU customer data needs to stay in EU regions. Can you guarantee region pinning for Private?
[07:09] Priya Patel: Yes — Private supports on-prem or VPC with region pinning. For Hosted we support region-aware routing; for strict residency we recommend Private deployment.
[07:22] Maya Thompson: One practical ask — can we get a sample dashboard CSV export of our demo metrics so we can plug into our finance model?
[07:28] Alex Chen: Absolutely — I'll attach a sample export and a small example spreadsheet mapping per-route cost into your finance model.

[07:36] Priya Patel: Back to console: here's the per-route traces view — you can jump from a spike to the request trace and inspect prompt, token count, and model latency. That helped another retailer track down a prompt that was accidentally sending full product descriptions as context.
[07:58] Daniel Park: Nice. For telemetry ingestion, what's the overhead? We don't want to double the request path latency by adding telemetry calls.
[08:04] Priya Patel: Telemetry is async; typical added p95 overhead is sub-millisecond. You can batch telemetry calls or ship via a sidecar to minimize impact.
[08:16] Maya Thompson: Are there any gotchas with our current infra — we run on EKS with API gateway and an internal caching layer.

[08:23] Priya Patel: EKS + API gateway is common. We'll provide best-practice integration guide (header tags, batching at gateway, TTLs for cache). One note: if you use multi-replica KV caches, enable sticky routing to reduce invalidation churn.
[08:40] Alex Chen: Competitors — have you evaluated any others?
[08:43] Maya Thompson: We looked at OpenAI for simplicity and Anthropic for safety, also did a quick eval of Vertex AI endpoints for infra integration.
[08:51] Alex Chen: Good context. Redwood focuses on predictable economics and production controls — consoles and Optimize try to close the loop between cost and quality.

[09:00] Priya Patel: I'm going to demo a quick 'what-if' scenario. I'm toggling caching for product_page from off to on — you can see simulated cost drop and expected latency improvement. This uses your uploaded telemetry if you provided it, otherwise a best-effort model.
[09:20] Maya Thompson: That simulated delta is really helpful for exec buy-in. Could you export the scenario as a PDF?
[09:25] Priya Patel: Yes, there's an export to PDF/CSV button. We'll include exports in the follow-up bundle.
[09:33] Sana Khan: From a procurement perspective, licensing for Dedicated — is there a minimum commitment?
[09:38] Alex Chen: We have starter tiers for small pilots (monthly) and recommend annual for larger Reserved pools. I'll put typical commitment sizes in the pricing doc.
[09:46] Daniel Park: For the benchmark, what data do you need us to send?
[09:50] Priya Patel: A sample of requests (anonymized prompts), token counts, and target QPS distribution. If you can send a one-week telemetry export, we'll run the per-route cost model against it.
[10:05] Maya Thompson: We can do that. We'll sanitize PII first.
[10:09] Alex Chen: Great. Quick time check — we've been demoing for about ten minutes, want to continue deeper into the Optimize section or save for follow-up?
[10:16] Maya Thompson: Continue Optimize briefly, please.

[10:18] Priya Patel: Sure. Optimize gives suggestions: batching windows, quantization recommendations per workload, cache TTL suggestions, and expected unit-cost delta. Here's an example: for short search queries, it recommends 32ms batching window with a small async queue to build batches at 120 qps, and suggests rwd-3b-quant for baseline with fallback to 13b for complex queries.
[10:45] Daniel Park: How do we validate quality impact of quantization? We can't risk degraded search relevance.
[10:50] Priya Patel: You can run A/B with golden prompts in Optimize, get automated metrics, and flag regressions. We also support human review exports for edge cases.
[11:02] Maya Thompson: Any limitations for on-prem Private deployment? We're curious about network VPC and hardware requirements.

[11:09] Priya Patel: Private has specific hardware SKUs we recommend (GPU types). We'll send a deployment checklist including NIC requirements and cluster sizing. For sensitive regulated workflows it's our recommended path.

[11:22] Alex Chen: Ok let's zoom out. Proposed pilot: 1-week benchmark running on a replicated traffic slice, Redwood runs per-route cost simulation and provides a report plus a recommended Dedicated sizing and cost-savings plan. Does that sound correct?
[11:33] Maya Thompson: Yes. We'd want to know the uplift or regression in latency and an estimated monthly spend at our scale.
[11:39] Alex Chen: Good. We'll also include SOC2 and network whitepaper, sample exports, and pricing ranges.
[11:45] Sana Khan: For procurement timelines — if the pilot shows good results, we could aim to commit by end of July. Finance needs a 30/60/90 day cost model.
[11:54] Alex Chen: Noted — we'll provide 30/60/90 scenarios in the pricing deck.
[12:00] Priya Patel: Any other technical blockers we should be aware of?
[12:03] Daniel Park: Nothing major. We just need to ensure telemetry is anonymized and the scripts run without touching PII.
[12:10] Priya Patel: Understood — we'll provide an anonymization guide. Also, we'll share a sample ingestion script for EKS sidecar.

[12:20] Alex Chen: Alright I'll do a quick recap of next steps and owners. Priya will run the benchmark plan and assemble scripts; I'll send pricing and SOC2 docs; Maya will share telemetry. Any objections?
[12:31] Maya Thompson: No objections, sounds good. One ask: can you include an example of cost per route mapped to our org teams? We want a chargeback-ready artifact.
[12:39] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll include a chargeback mapping example in the export bundle.
[12:44] Sana Khan: Thanks — appreciate the clarity.
[12:47] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck, SOC2, sample CSVs, and the benchmark plan. We'll schedule the kickoff after telemetry is uploaded. Bye all.
[57:30] (call ends)
